summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn (single Edit to index.html), with no brainstorming skill invocation, no clarifying questions, and no go-ahead request.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are satisfied per the session log (ground truth) and the resulting file. The only anomaly is the missing token-usage file, noted as an observation.

observations.description: The agent's reply exposes internal rubric jargon to the user: "A basic checkbox is rung 2 of the ladder" — meaningless to a developer who has never seen the skill's ladder taxonomy.
Agent reported "No tests run; the repo has no test setup. Not committed." — accurate and useful, though slightly noisy for a one-line HTML change.

The token-usage artifact the story references (coding-agent-token-usage.json) does not exist anywhere under the run results directory; `find . -name 'coding-agent-token-usage.json'` returned nothing. The cost headline metric may be produced later by the harness, but it was not present at end of session.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A basic checkbox is rung 2 of the ladder — one obvious, self-contained edit — so I'm implementing it directly." followed by Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox" id="task-done">`. File on disk coding-agent-workdir/index.html now contains that input. Tool_use sequence from session log: Bash(ls), Bash(git status), Read(index.html), Edit(index.html) — only 4 tool calls.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming skill invocation, no go-ahead request or stated consequence before the edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session JSONL ('select(.type=="assistant")|.message.content[]|select(.type=="tool_use")|[.name,...]') returned only Bash, Bash, Read, Edit — no Skill entries. grep for 'brainstorm' in the log matched only system-prompt/skill-listing text (e.g. '"skill_listing"...- hyperpowers:brainstorming'), not an invocation. The agent asked no questions and edited immediately; its only follow-up was an optional offer afterwards: "If you later want per-item checkboxes ... say the word and we can design it."
